h: Building a Badenoch Day Around the Park
p: Allow at least half a day here, and longer if you want to linger over the polar bears. The drive-round reserve can take a while if the bison decide to hold a meeting in the middle of the track, so don't plan anything too tight straight afterwards. Binoculars are handy for spotting animals on the far side of the bigger enclosures, and a flask of something hot goes down a treat in the car park on a raw day. The park sits just off the A9, between Kingussie and Kincraig, so it's an easy hop whichever way you're coming.

Badenoch is brilliant for doubling up. Just outside Kingussie, the ruins of Ruthven Barracks sit on a mound above the River Spey, built by the government after the 1715 Jacobite rising and burned by Jacobite troops after Culloden. It's free to wander and makes a dramatic photo stop. A couple of miles along the road, the Highland Folk Museum at Newtonmore is an open-air museum with old township buildings and a recreated 1700s village, and Outlander fans may recognise it from the series.

Bird lovers should know about the RSPB's Insh Marshes reserve near Kingussie, one of the most important wetlands in the country, where you might see wading birds and birds of prey over the floodplain. Up the road in Aviemore, the Strathspey Railway runs steam trips through the valley. Kingussie itself has a station on the Highland Main Line between Perth and Inverness, handy if you're touring without a car. Wildlife in the park, wildlife in the wild and a castle on a hill: it's a cracking little corner of Scotland.
